hook: GitHub just released an AI prototyping tool under MIT.

sections.voiceover: GitHub just released an AI prototyping tool under MIT.
sections.visual_cue: GitHub logo with the word “Replica” and a MIT license badge.

sections.voiceover: On October 28, 2026, GitHub Design open‑sourced Replica, an AI‑powered prototyping tool. It runs in Copilot and ships under the MIT license. Does the 2‑minute read cover all the steps?
sections.visual_cue: Timeline showing Oct 28 2026, then a screenshot of Replica in Copilot, then a 2‑minute read icon with a question mark.

sections.voiceover: But it only works with components you already have, not new ones.
sections.visual_cue: Split‑screen comparison: left side shows existing repo components, right side shows empty new components.

sections.voiceover: The GitHub blog offers a 2‑minute read guide to launch Replica. Developers can pull the MIT‑licensed code from the public repository today. Once integrated, teams instantly generate interactive prototypes inside Copilot without extra licensing fees.
sections.visual_cue: Blog page with 2‑minute read badge, then GitHub repo page, then Copilot UI creating a prototype.

sections.voiceover: Free, open‑source prototyping now at your fingertips.
sections.visual_cue: Hand reaching toward a glowing “Free” button over the Replica logo.
